chunks: And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
Indeed, for every salat there are two times, except for Maghrib — for its time is one, and its time is its obligation, and the time of its expiry is the falling of the twilight redness.
And it is also narrated that for it there are two times, the last of its time being the falling of the twilight redness.

And this does not contradict the first hadith [stating] that it has one time, because the twilight redness (shafaq) is the redness (humra), and between the setting of the sun and the disappearance of the twilight redness there is only a small thing — and that is that the sign of the sun's setting is when the redness reaches the direction of qibla, and between the redness reaching the qibla and its disappearance there is only the measure of time in which a person can pray Maghrib and its nawafil when he prays them with deliberateness and tranquillity. And I have observed this more than once, and that is why the time of Maghrib is narrow.

key_terms.الشَّفَق: Twilight redness (shafaq) — the red glow on the horizon after sunset; its disappearance marks the end of Maghrib time
key_terms.الْحُمْرَة: Redness — the same phenomenon as shafaq; al-Kulayni identifies the two as identical
key_terms.الْقِبْلَة: Qibla — the direction of prayer (toward Mecca); here used as an astronomical reference point
key_terms.نَوَافِل: Nawafil — the voluntary/recommended prayers performed after the obligatory Maghrib salat
key_terms.وُجُوبُهَا: Its obligation — the moment the salat becomes obligatory (i.e., the beginning of its time)

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Maghrib prayer begin and end according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that each salat has two times except Maghrib, whose time begins with its obligation at sunset. He resolves an apparent contradiction between narrations by explaining that the twilight redness (shafaq) used as the expiry marker is nearly simultaneous with sunset — the interval being only as long as it takes to pray Maghrib with its nawafil at a calm pace. The closing remark ('I have observed this more than once, and that is why the time of Maghrib is narrow') is believed to be a clarifying gloss by al-Kulayni himself, not part of the original hadith.

en.hubeali: And it is reported from Zurara and Al Fuzayl who both said, ‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘For every Salāt are two timings apart from Al-Maghrib. So it’s time is one, and its time is its Obligatory time, and the time for its expiry is the falling of the redness (from sight)’. And it is reported as well that for it are two timings, the last of its timing being the falling of the redness (from sight)’. And this is not from what opposes the first Hadeeth. For it is one timing, because the twilight, it is the redness, and there is not between the setting of the sun and the setting of the redness except for a small thing, and that is that a sign of the setting of the sun is when the redness reaches overhead, and there is not between the reaching of the redness overhead and its disappearance except for a measurement of what the human being would pray the Maghrib Salāt and its Optional, when he prays it upon unhurriedness and tranquillity, and I have surveyed it many a time, and it is due to that, then time for Al-Maghrib is narrow’. (P.S. – This is not part of the Hadeeth and looks like a comment to me, probably from Kulayni himself).
en.sarwar: 9. He has narrated it from Zurarah and al-Fudayl who have said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,

‘For every Salah (prayer) there are two timings except al- Maghrib; its timing is one and it is the time when it becomes obligatory. It ends with the disappearance of al-Shafaq (redness in the west).”’
“It is also narrated that there are two timings for al-Maghrib and it ends with the disappearance of al- Shafaq (redness).

It does not disagree with the previous Hadith that says it has one time; because al- Shafaq is the redness. The time between sunset and disappearance of al-Shafaq is not very long. The sign of sunset is when redness reaches past one’s overhead when facing the direction of sunset, and it is a short time. The time between the reaching of the redness in the western horizon and its disappearance is not more than a time that takes one to complete al-Maghrib Salah (prayer) and its Nawafil (optional) Salah (prayer), if they are performed comfortably. I have examined it many times and for this reason the timing for al-Maghrib is narrow.”
